);\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_cpu_load_avg\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"System load average over 15 minutes\",\n            \"window=\\\"15m\\\"\",\n            self.cpu.load_avg[2]\n        );\n\n        // --- Memory Metrics ---\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_total_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Total physical memory in    \"counter\",\n                \"Total completed write operations\",\n                labels,\n                disk.writes_total\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_disk_read_bytes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total bytes read\",\n                labels,\n                disk.read_bytes\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_disk_write_bytes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total bytes written\",\n                labels,\n                disk.write_bytes\n            );\n        }\n\n        // --- Network Metrics ---\n        for net in \u0026self.networks {\n            let labels = format!(\"interface=\\\"{}\\\"\", net.interface);\n            metric!(\n    clippy::unwrap_used,\n    clippy::expect_used,\n    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,\n    clippy::identity_op\n)]\n//! Identity-mapped x86-64 page table generation.\n//!\n//! Builds 4-level page tables using 2 MiB huge pages. The output is a\n//! sequence of [`MemWrite`] chunks that the caller writes into guest\n//! physical memory — `hitz-boot` never touches guest RAM directly.\n\nuse hitz_hal::Gpa;\n\nuse crate::error::BootError;\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Public types\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// A chunk of data to write into guest memory.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct MemWrite {\n    /// Guest physical address where the data should be written.\n    pub gpa: Gpa,\n    /// Raw bytes to write at `gpa`.\n    pub data: Vec\u003cu8\u003e,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Constants\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Guest physical address of the PML4 table.\npub const PML4_GPA: u64 = 0x8000;\n/// Guest physical address of the PDPT table.\npub const PDPT_GPA: u64 = 0x9000;\n/// Guest physical address of the first Page Directory table.\npub const PD_BASE_GPA: u64 = 0xA000;\n\n/// Page is present in memory.\nconst PAGE_PRESENT: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 0;\n/// Page is read/write.\nconst PAGE_RW: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 1;\n/// PS bit — marks a 2 MiB huge page in a PD entry.\nconst PAGE_SIZE_FLAG: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 7;\n\n/// Flags for a table entry that points to a child table (PML4 -\u003e PDPT, PDPT -\u003e PD).\nconst TABLE_FLAGS: u64 = PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_RW; // 0x3\n/// Flags for a 2 MiB huge page leaf entry in a PD table.\nconst HUGE_PAGE_FLAGS: u64 = PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_RW | PAGE_SIZE_FLAG; // 0x83\n\n/// Size of a single page table (4 KiB).\nconst PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;\n/// Number of 8-byte entries per page table.\nconst ENTRIES_PER_TABLE: usize = 512;\n/// Size of a 2 MiB huge page in bytes.\nconst HUGE_PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 2 * 1024 * 1024;\n/// Size of 1 GiB in bytes.\nconst ONE_GIB: u64 = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;\n/// Maximum GiB count supported (PDPT has 512 entries, each mapping 1 GiB).\nconst MAX_GIB: u32 = 512;\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Public API\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Build identity-mapped page tables for `gib_count` GiB of physical memory.\n///\n/// Returns `(pml4_gpa, writes)` where `pml4_gpa` is the address to load into\n/// CR3 and `writes` is the set of page-table pages to write into guest RAM.\n///\n/// Uses 2 MiB huge pages so only three levels are needed:\n/// PML4 -\u003e PDPT -\u003e PD (with PS bit set).\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns [`BootError::InvalidPageTableConfig`] if `gib_count` is zero or\n/// exceeds 512 (the maximum a single PDPT can map).\npub fn build_page_tables(gib_count: u32) -\u003e Result\u003c(Gpa, Vec\u003cMemWrite\u003e), BootError\u003e {\n    if gib_count == 0 || gib_count \u003e MAX_GIB {\n        return Err(BootError::InvalidPageTableConfig(format!(\n            \"gib_count must be in 1..={MAX_GIB}, got {gib_count}\"\n        )));\n    }\n\n    // Total writes: 1 PML4 + 1 PDPT + gib_count PD tables.\n    let total_writes = 2 + gib_count as usize;\n    let mut writes = Vec::with_capacity(total_writes);\n\n    // -- PML4 (one entry pointing at the PDPT) ----------------------------\n    let mut pml4 = vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE];\n    write_entry(\u0026mut pml4, 0, PDPT_GPA | TABLE_FLAGS);\n    writes.push(MemWrite {\n        gpa: Gpa::new(PML4_GPA),\n        data: pml4,\n    });\n\n    // -- PDPT (one entry per GiB, each pointing at a PD table) ------------\n    let mut pdpt = vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE];\n    for i in 0..gib_count {\n        let pd_gpa = PD_BASE_GPA + u64::from(i) * PAGE_SIZE as u64;\n        write_entry(\u0026mut pdpt, i as usize, pd_gpa | TABLE_FLAGS);\n    }\n    writes.push(MemWrite {\n        gpa: Gpa::new(PDPT_GPA),\n        data: pdpt,\n    });\n\n    // -- PD tables (512 x 2 MiB huge-page entries each) -------------------\n    for i in 0..gib_count {\n        let mut pd = vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE];\n        for j in 0..ENTRIES_PER_TABLE {\n            let phys_addr = u64::from(i) * ONE_GIB + j as u64 * HUGE_PAGE_SIZE;\n            write_entry(\u0026mut pd, j, phys_addr | HUGE_PAGE_FLAGS);\n        }\n        writes.push(MemWrite {\n            gpa: Gpa::new(PD_BASE_GPA + u64::from(i) * PAGE_SIZE as u64),\n            data: pd,\n        });\n    }\n\n    Ok((Gpa::new(PML4_GPA), writes))\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Write a 64-bit little-endian value into the `index`-th slot of a page table.\nfn write_entry(table: \u0026mut [u8], index: usize, value: u64) {\n    let offset = index * 8;\n    table[offset..offset + 8].copy_from_slice(\u0026value.to_le_bytes());\n}\n\n/// Read a 64-bit little-endian value from the `index`-th slot of a page table.\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn read_entry(table: \u0026[u8], index: usize) -\u003e u64 {\n    let offset = index * 8;\n    u64::from_le_bytes(table[offset..offset + 8].try_into().expect(\"8 bytes\"))\n}\n\n// use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_4gib_page_tables() {\n        let (cr3, writes) = build_page_tables(4).expect(\"4 GiB should succeed\");\n\n        // 1 PML4 + 1 PDPT + 4 PD = 6 writes\n      completion_tx: tx,\n            completion_rx: Arc::new(tokio::sync::Mutex::new(rx)),\n            vm_count,\n            shutdown_rx,\n            shutdown_tx_owned: Arc::new(shutdown_tx),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Clones an existing VM configuration into a new VM.\n    ///\n    /// The source VM can be in any state. The new VM will be created in the `Created` state,\n    /// identical in configuration to the source, but with the new `dest_id`.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns a [`DaemonError`] if the source VM does not exist, or if the destination\n    /// VM ID already exists.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// manager.clone_vm(\"my-vm\", \"my-vm-clone\").expect(\"Failed to clone VM\");\n    /// ```\n    pub fn clone_vm(\u0026self, src_id: \u0026str, dest_id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let config = {\n            self.vms\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?\n                .get(src_id)\n                .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(src_id.to_string()))?\n                .config\n                .clone()\n        };\n\n        self.create_vm(dest_id.to_string(), \u0026config)\n    }\n\n    /// Wires the vsock metrics tasks to stop when a daemon-provided shutdown signal fires.\n    ///\n    /// **Why do we need a shutdown receiver?**\n    /// A running VM might have a background task pumping metrics over a vsock channel.\n    /// If the daemon needs to shut down cleanly, it must signal these background tasks\n    /// to exit their polling loops; otherwise, the Tokio runtime will hang waiting for them.\n    ///\n    /// Call this after constructing the manager. If not called, the manager uses a dummy internal\n    /// channel that never fires, which is acceptable for standalone or test execution.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let mut manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// let (shutdown_tx, shutdown_rx) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(false);\n    /// manager.set_shutdown_receiver(shutdown_rx);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn set_shutdown_receiver(\u0026mut self, rx: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver\u003cbool\u003e) {\n        self.shutdown_rx = rx;\n    }\n\n    /// Creates a VM with the given ID and configuration.\n    ///\n    /// This validates the [`VmConfig`] and persists it to disk. It does **not** boot the VM.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns a [`DaemonError`] if a VM with the same ID already exists, if the configuration\n    /// is invalid, or if the state \u0026config).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn create_vm(\u0026self, id: String, config: \u0026VmConfig) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        if id.contains('/') || id.contains('\\\\') || id.contains(\"..\") {\n            return Err(DaemonError::Internal(\"Invalid VM ID\".to_string()));\n        }\n\n        hitz_vmm::validate_config(config)?;\n\n        let info = {\n            let mut vms = self\n                .vms\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n\n            if vms.contains_key(\u0026id) {\n                return Err(DaemonError::AlreadyExists(id));\n            }\n\n            let entry = VmEntry {\n                config: config.clone(),\n info = entry.to_info(\u0026id);\n            let _ = vms.insert(id.clone(), entry);\n            info\n            // Mutex released here — filesystem I/O must not hold it.\n        };\n\n        if in-memory insert so a retry doesn't hit AlreadyExists.\n            if let Ok(mut vms) = self.vms.lock() {\n                let _ = vms.remove(\u0026id);\n            }\n            return Err(e);\n        }\n        Ok(info)\n    }\n\n    /// Boots a previously created VM.\n    ///\n    /// Transitions a `Created` VM into the `Running` state. ```\n    #[allow(clippy::significant_drop_tightening, clippy::too_many_lines)]\n    pub fn start_vm(\u0026self, id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let (config, stop_flag, serial_buf, info) = {\n            let mut vms = self\n                .vms\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n            let entry = vms\n                .get_mut(id)\n                .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(id.to_string()))?;\n\n            if entry.state != VmState::Created {\n                return Err(DaemonError::InvalidState {\n                    id: id.to_string(),\n                    state: entry.state,\n                    expected: \"Created\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n\n            let flag = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));\n            entry.stop_flag = Some(flag.clone());\n            entry.state = VmState::Running;\n\n            let serial_buf = SerialBuf::new();\n            entry.serial_buf = Some(serial_buf.clone());\n\n            (entry.config.clone(), flag, serial_buf, entry.to_info(id))\n        };\n        // Mutex released here — spawn_blocking must not hold it.\n\n        // Persist Running state before spawning the VM task.\n        self.store.save_state(id, VmState::Running)?;\n\n        // Inject guest agent overlay into initramfs if agent is enabled.\n        let boot_config = inject_guest_agent(config, id);\n\n        // Record guest RAM size as a one-shot gauge.\n        {\n            let meter = opentelemetry::global::meter(\"hitz\");\n            let memory_gauge = meter\n                .u64_gauge(\"hitz.vm.memory_bytes\")\n                .with_description(\"Guest RAM in bytes at VM start\")\n                .build();\n            memory_gauge.record(\n                u64::from(boot_config.ram_mib) * 1024 * 1024,\n                \u0026[KeyValue::new(\"vm.id\", id.to_string())],\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Increment the running-VM count.\n        self.vm_count.add(1, \u0026[KeyValue::new(\"state\", \"running\")]);\n\n        let hv = self.hypervisor.clone();\n        let vms = self.vms.clone();\n        let vm_id = id.to_string();\n        let completion_tx = self.completion_tx.clone();\n        let vm_count_clone = Arc::clone(\u0026self.vm_count);\n        let vm_id_span = vm_id.clone();\n\n        // Create vsock channels if agent injection is enabled.\n        // The host-facing ends are consumed by the async metrics task;\n        // the device-facing ends are passed to boot_and_run via BootExtras.\n        // On-demand pull is a future enhancement; only push-to-OTel is wired here.\n        let extras = if matches!(\n            boot_config.guest_agent,\n            hitz_api::GuestAgentMode::Auto | hitz_api::GuestAgentMode::Custom(_)\n        ) {\n            let (handle, rx_receiver, tx_sender) = hitz_vmm::VsockIoHandle::new_pair();\n            // Spawn the async metrics task with the host-facing channel ends.\n            // The task runs until the channels close (VM exit) or shutdown.\n            let shutdown_rx = self.shutdown_rx.clone();\n            drop(tokio::spawn(crate::vsock_server::run_metrics_task(\n                vm_id.clone(),\n                handle.tx_rx,\n                handle.rx_tx,\n                shutdown_rx,\n            )));\n            hitz_vmm::BootExtras {\n                vsock_channels: Some((rx_receiver, tx_sender)),\n            }\n        } else {\n            hitz_vmm::BootExtras::none()\n        };\n\n        let store_exit = Arc::clone(\u0026self.store);\n\n        // Fire-and-forget: the spawned task updates VM state on completion\n        // and signals the completion channel so `stop_all_and_wait` can drain.\n        drop(tokio::task::spawn(async move {\n            let boot_span = tracing::info_span!(\n                \"vm.boot\",\n                vm.id = %vm_id_span,\n                vm.ram_mib = boot_config.ram_mib,\n                vm.cpus = boot_config.cpus,\n            );\n            let _boot_enter = boot_span.enter();\n\n            // Start port forwarders if networking is configured and rules exist.\n            let _port_fwd = start_port_forwarding(\u0026boot_config).await;\n\n            let result = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {\n                hitz_vmm::boot_and_run(\u0026*hv, \u0026boot_config, serial_buf, stop_flag, extras)\n            })\n            .await;\n\n            // _port_fwd drops here → all listener tasks aborted.\n\n            // Decrement the running-VM count now that the VM has exited.\n            vm_count_clone.add(-1, \u0026[KeyValue::new(\"state\", \"running\")]);\n\n            // Update state based on result.\n            if let Ok(mut vms) = vms.lock() {\n                if let Some(entry) = vms.get_mut(\u0026vm_id) {\n                    match result {\n                        Ok(Ok(run_result)) =\u003e match run_result.exit_reason {\n                            ExitReason::Halt | ExitReason::Shutdown | ExitReason::Canceled =\u003e {\n                                entry.state = VmState::Stopped;\n                                entry.exit_reason = Some(format!(\"{:?}\", run_result.exit_reason));\n                            }\n                            ExitReason::Unexpected(ref reason) =\u003e {\n                                entry.state = VmState::Failed;\n                                entry.exit_reason = Some(reason.clone());\n                            }\n                        },\n                        Ok(Err(e)) =\u003e {\n                            entry.state = VmState::Failed;\n                            entry.exit_reason = Some(e.to_string());\n                        }\n                        Err(e) =\u003e {\n                            entry.state = VmState::Failed;\n                            entry.exit_reason = Some(format!(\"task panicked: {e}\"));\n                        }\n                    }\n                    entry.stop_flag = None;\n                    entry.vsock_handle = None;\n                    if let Some(ref buf) = entry.serial_buf {\n                        buf.close();\n                    }\n                    let final_state = entry.state;\n                    drop(vms); // explicit drop — persist state outside the lock\n                    if let Err(e) = store_exit.save_state(\u0026vm_id, final_state) {\n                        tracing::warn!(vm_id = %vm_id, error = %e, \"failed to persist VM exit state\");\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Notify stop_all_and_wait that this VM has finished.\n            let _ = completion_tx.send(vm_id);\n        }));\n\n        Ok(info)\n    }\n\n    /// Stops a running VM by setting its atomic stop flag.\n    ///\n    /// **Why an atomic flag?**\n    /// The vCPU is deeply buried inside a synchronous run loop on a separate thread.\n    /// We can't simply `await` it to stop. Instead, we flip an atomic boolean.\n    /// A cancel-watchdog thread checks this flag and issues a hypervisor-level cancellation\n    /// to yank the vCPU back to reality.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, self\n            .vms\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n        let entry = vms\n            .get_mut(id)\n            .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(id.to_string()))?;\n\n        if entry.state != VmState::Running {\n            return Err(DaemonError::InvalidState {\n                id: id.to_string(),\n                state: entry.state,\n                expected: \"Running\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref flag) = entry.stop_flag {\n            flag.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        }\n\n        let info = entry.to_info(id);\n        drop(vms);\n        Ok(info)\n    }\n\n    /// Restarts a running VM by stopping it, waiting for it to stop, and then starting it again.\n    pub async fn restart_vm(\u0026self, id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let _ = self.stop_vm(id)?;\n\n        let mut stopped = false;\n \"VM {id} failed to stop within 5 seconds for restart\"\n            )));\n        }\n\n        self.start_vm(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Gets a serial output reader for a running VM.\n    ///\n    /// When the VM is stopped\n    /// or hasn't started, the buffer doesn't exist.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// let mut reader = manager.serial_reader(\"my-vm\").unwrap();\n    /// // Stream chunks to the client...\n    /// ```\n    pub fn serial_reader(\u0026self, id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cSerialReader, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let vms = self\n            .vms\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n        let entry = vms\n            .get(id)\n            .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(id.to_string()))?;\n        let reader = entry\n            .serial_buf\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(SerialBuf::reader)\n            .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::InvalidState {\n                id: id.to_string(),\n                state: entry.state,\n                expected: \"Running (with serial buffer)\".to_string(),\n            })?;\n        drop(vms);\n        Ok(reader)\n    }\n\n    /// Gets detailed information about a single VM.\n    ///\n    /// ## Returns immediately without waiting\n    /// for the VMs to reach a terminal state.\n    ///\n    /// Use [`VmManager::stop_all_and_wait`] if you need to block until all VMs have stopped.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// use std::time::Duration;\n    /// # let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build().unwrap();\n    /// # rt.block_on(async {\n    /// manager.stop_all_and_wait(Duration::from_secs(5)).await;\n    /// # });\n    /// ```\n    pub async fn stop_all_and_wait(\u0026self, timeout: Duration) {\n        let running_count = {\n            let Ok(vms) = self.vms.lock() else { return };\n            let mut count = 0usize;\n            for entry in vms.values() {\n                if entry.state == VmState::Running {\n                    if let Some(ref flag) = entry.stop_flag {\n                        flag.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n                    }\n                    count += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            count\n        };\n\n        if running_count == 0 {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(running_count, \"waiting for VMs to stop\");\n\n        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + timeout;\n        let mut rx = self.completion_rx.lock().await;\n        let mut stopped = 0usize;\n\n        while stopped \u003c running_count {\n            match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, rx.recv()).await {\n                Ok(Some(_vm_id)) =\u003e {\n                    stopped += 1;\n                }\n                Ok(None) =\u003e break, // channel closed — no more senders\n                Err(_elapsed) =\u003e {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        remaining = running_count - stopped,\n                        \"timeout waiting for VMs to stop\"\n                    );\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// On-demand metrics pull. response — requires storing a dedicated pull channel end in\n    /// `VmEntry` separate from the push stream read by `run_metrics_task`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn request_metrics_snapshot(\n Currently supported devices include a 16550A-compatible serial console ([`SerialDevice`]),\n//! a virtio-block storage backend ([`VirtioBlockDevice`]), and a virtio-net network interface ([`VirtioNetDevice`]).\n//!\n//! # The Hero's Journey\n//!\n//! Devices are instantiated during the VM setup phase and registered with the central `MmioBus`.\n//! Here is a simplified illustration of how devices are attached to the bus:\n//!\n//! ```no_run\n//! use hitz_devices::{MmioBus, SerialDevice, VirtioBlockDevice, VirtioMmioTransport};\n//! use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n//!\n//! // 1. Create devices\n//! let mut serial = SerialDevice::new(std::io::sink());\n//! let block_backend = VirtioBlockDevice::new(std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/null\").unwrap()).unwrap();\n//! let mut block_device = VirtioMmioTransport::new(block_backend, std::sync::Arc::new(DummyMem), 5);\n//!\n\n//! // 3. When a guest access occurs (intercepted by WHP), route it:\n//! // e.g., guest writes 'A' (0x41) to the serial port\n//! bus.write(0x3f8, \u0026[0x41], \u0026DummyMem);\n//! ```\n//!\n//! # The Fine Print\n//!\n//! - **Virtio Over MMIO**: Hitz prefers the virtio-MMIO transport over PCI for simplicity\n//!   and reduced surface area. The kernel must be compiled with `CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO`\n//!   enabled, and device memory regions must be passed to the kernel via command line\n//! Device ID: 1 (virtio net device).\n\nuse std::collections::VecDeque;\n\nuse crossbeam_channel::{Receiver, Sender};\nuse hitz_hal::GuestMemAccess;\n\nuse crate::virtio::mmio_transport::VirtioBackend;\nuse crate::virtio::queue::VirtQueue;\n\n/// Size of the virtio-net header prepended to every frame.\nconst VIRTIO_NET_HDR_SIZE: usize = 12;\n\n/// Feature bit: device has a given MAC address in config space.\nconst VIRTIO_NET_F_MAC: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 5;\n\n/// RX virtqueue index (guest receives frames here).\nconst RX_QUEUE: u16 = 0;\n\n/// TX virtqueue index (guest sends frames here).\nconst TX_QUEUE: u16 = 1;\n\n/// A virtio-net device implementation.\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Provides a paravirtualized network interface to the guest OS. It uses two\n/// virtqueues: one for receiving packets (RX) and one for transmitting packets (TX).\n///\n/// This structure bridges the guest's memory buffers with host-side crossbeam\n/// channels, allowing an asynchronous host network thread to inject received ethernet\n/// frames and drain transmitted frames.\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use hitz_devices::VirtioNetDevice;\n/// # use crossbeam_channel::unbounded;\n/// # use hitz_devices::VirtioMmioTransport;\n/// # use hitz_hal::GuestMemAccess;\n/// # use std::sync::Arc;\n/// # struct DummyMem;\n/// # impl GuestMemAccess for DummyMem {\n/// #     fn read_guest(\u0026self, _gpa: u64, _buf: \u0026mut [u8]) -\u003e Result\u003c(), hitz_hal::HalError\u003e { Ok(()) }\n/// #     fn write_guest(\u0026self, _gpa: u64, _data: \u0026[u8]) -\u003e Result\u003c(), hitz_hal::HalError\u003e { Ok(()) }\n/// # }\n/// // 1. GuestMemAccess) {\n        // ⚡ Bolt: Hoist buffer to eliminate multiple heap allocations per transmitted frame.\n        let mut frame_data = Vec::with_capacity(2048);\n        while let Some(mut chain) = queue.pop_chain(mem) {\n            let head = chain.head_index();\n            frame_data.clear();\n\n            // Collect all device-readable buffers in the chain.\n            while let Some(desc) = chain.next_descriptor(mem) {\n                if !desc.is_device_writable {\n                    let start_len = frame_data.len();\n                    frame_data.resize(start_len + -\u003e bool {\n        let Some(raw_frame) = self.rx_pending.front() else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        let Some(mut chain) = queue.pop_chain(mem) else {\n            return Shared types for the HAL: exit reasons, register state, configuration.\n\nuse crate::newtypes::{Gpa, MemSizeMiB, VcpuId};\n\n/// Configuration for creating a new partition.\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Defines the fundamental parameters required to bootstrap a new VM.\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use hitz_hal::{PartitionConfig, MemSizeMiB};\n///\n/// let config = PartitionConfig {\n///     vcpu_count: 2,\n///     memory_size: MemSizeMiB::new(1024),\n/// };\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Represents the various reasons a virtual CPU might stop execution\n/// and return control to the Virtual Machine Monitor (VMM).\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use hitz_hal::VcpuExit;\n///\n/// fn handle_exit(exit: VcpuExit) {\n///     match exit {\n///         VcpuExit::Halt =\u003e println!(\"Guest halted\"),\n///         VcpuExit::Shutdown =\u003e println!(\"Guest shutting down\"),\n///         _ =\u003e println!(\"Other exit reason\"),\n///     }\n/// }\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum VcpuExit {\n    /// Guest performed an MMIO access.\n    Mmio(MmioExit),\n    /// Guest performed an I/O port access (IN/OUT instruction).\n    IoPort(IoPortExit),\n    /// Guest executed HLT.\n    Halt,\n    /// vCPU is ready to accept an interrupt injection.\n    InterruptWindow,\n    /// vCPU run was canceled via [`Vcpu::cancel`](crate::Vcpu::cancel).\n    Canceled,\n    /// Guest initiated shutdown (triple fault, etc.).\n    Shutdown,\n    /// Exit reason not recognized by this HAL version.\n    Unknown(u32),\n}\n\n/// Details of an MMIO exit.\n///\n/// # For smaller accesses, only the lower bytes are valid.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct MmioExit {\n    /// Guest physical address being accessed.\n    pub gpa: Gpa,\n    /// Data buffer — for writes, contains the value written by the guest.\n    /// For reads, the VMM fills this before resuming.\n    pub data: [u8; Sets up the vCPU in 64-bit long mode with identity-mapped page tables,\n//! a minimal GDT, and the entry point / `boot_params` pointer expected by\n//! the Linux boot protocol.\n\nuse hitz_hal::{DescriptorTable, Gpa, SegmentDescriptor, SpecialRegs, StandardRegs, Vcpu};\n\nuse crate::error::MemError;\nuse crate::memory::GuestMemory;\n\n// ─── GDT layout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Guest physical address where the GDT is placed.\npub const GDT_GPA: u64 = 0x500;\n\n/// Null descriptor (required first entry).\nconst GDT_NULL: u64 = 0;\n\n/// 64-bit code segment descriptor.\n///\n/// Base=0, Limit=0xFFFFF, Type=0xB (exec/read/accessed), S=1, DPL=0,\n/// P=1, L=1 (long mode), D=0, G=1.\n///\n/// Raw: `0x00AF_9B00_0000_FFFF`\nconst GDT_CODE64: u64 = 0x00AF_9B00_0000_FFFF;\n\n/// 64-bit data segment descriptor.\n///\n/// Base=0, Limit=0xFFFFF, Type=0x3 (read/write/accessed), S=1, DPL=0,\n/// P=1, L=0, D=1 (32-bit default ops for data), G=1.\n///\n/// Raw: `0x00CF_9300_0000_FFFF`\nconst GDT_DATA64: u64 = 0x00CF_9300_0000_FFFF;\n\n/// Selector for the 64-bit code segment (entry 1 in GDT, ring 0).\nconst CS_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;\n/// Selector for the 64-bit data segment (entry 2 in GDT, ring 0).\nconst DS_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x10;\n/// Selector for the TSS descriptor (entry 3 in GDT, ring 0).\nconst TR_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x18;\n\n/// Number of GDT entries: null + code64 + data64 + TSS low.\n///\n/// A 64-bit TSS descriptor occupies TWO GDT slots (16 bytes) but we only\n/// need the low 8 bytes in the GDT — the high 8 bytes encode the upper\n/// 32 bits of base which is 0 for us.\nconst GDT_ENTRY_COUNT: usize = 5; // null, code64, data64, tss_low, tss_high\n/// Size of each GDT entry in bytes.\nconst GDT_ENTRY_SIZE: usize = 8;\n\n/// Guest physical address of the minimal 64-bit TSS.\n///\n/// Placed right after the GDT (5 entries * 8 bytes = 40 bytes starting at 0x500,\n/// so TSS at 0x528). The TSS is zero-initialized by the guest memory allocator.\npub const TSS_GPA: u64 = GDT_GPA + (GDT_ENTRY_COUNT as u64) * (GDT_ENTRY_SIZE as u64);\n\n/// Size of a minimal 64-bit TSS (104 bytes = 0x68).\nconst TSS_SIZE: u64 = 0x68;\n\n// ─── Control register values for 64-bit long mode ───────────────────────────\n\n/// CR0: PE + MP + ET + NE + WP + AM + PG.\n///\n/// WHP requires more than the bare minimum for long mode. In particular,\n/// NE (numeric error handling, bit 5) and the FPU/SSE-related bits must\n/// be set for the vCPU state to be considered valid.\nconst CR0_LONG_MODE: u64 = (1 \u003c\u003c 0)  // PE  — protection enable\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 1)                        // MP  — monitor coprocessor\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 4)                        // ET  — extension type\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 5)                        // NE  — numeric error\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 16)                       // WP  — write protect\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 18)                       // AM  — alignment mask\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 31); // PG  — paging\n// = 0x8005_0033\n\n/// CR4: PAE + OSFXSR + OSXMMEXCPT.\n///\n/// PAE is required for long mode. OSFXSR and OSXMMEXCPT enable SSE\n/// support, which WHP expects for a valid 64-bit register state.\nconst CR4_LONG_MODE: u64 = (1 \u003c\u003c 5)  // PAE — physical address extension\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 9)                        // OSFXSR — OS support for FXSAVE/FXRSTOR\n    | (1 \u003c\u003c 10); // OSXMMEXCPT — OS support for unmasked SIMD FP exceptions\n// = 0x620\n\n/// EFER: LME (long mode enable) + LMA (long mode active).\n/// When PG is set in CR0 with LME in EFER, the CPU activates LMA automatically.\n/// We set both explicitly since WHP expects the VMM to provide the full state.\nconst EFER_LONG_MODE: u64 = (1 \u003c\u003c 8) | (1 \u003c\u003c 10); // 0x500\n\n/// RFLAGS: bit 1 is always reserved/set on x86.\nconst RFLAGS_INIT: u64 = 0x2;\n\n// ─── Segment descriptor helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Decode an 8-byte raw GDT entry into a HAL `SegmentDescriptor`.\nconst fn decode_gdt_entry(raw: u64, selector: u16) -\u003e SegmentDescriptor {\n    // Base: bits [31:24] \u003c\u003c 24 | bits [39:32] \u003c\u003c 16 | bits [15:0] of the high half\n    // For flat segments (base=0, which is our case), this is all zeros.\n    let base_low = (raw \u003e\u003e 16) \u0026 0xFFFF;\n    let base_mid = (raw \u003e\u003e 32) \u0026 0xFF;\n    let base_high = (raw \u003e\u003e 56) \u0026 0xFF;\n    let base = (base_high \u003c\u003c 24) | (base_mid \u003c\u003c 16) | base_low;\n\n    // Limit: bits [19:16] from byte 6 high nibble, bits [15:0] from low word\n    let limit_low = raw \u0026 0xFFFF;\n    let limit_high = (raw \u003e\u003e 48) \u0026 0x0F;\n    // If granularity bit is set, limit is in 4 KiB units -\u003e shift left 12 and OR 0xFFF.\n    let granularity = ((raw \u003e\u003e 55) \u0026 1) as u8;\n    let limit_raw = (limit_high \u003c\u003c 16) | limit_low;\n    // Limit fits in 20 bits (max 0xFFFFF). With granularity, shifted left 12\n    // gives at most 0xFFFF_FFFF which fits u32.\n    #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]\n    let limit = if granularity == 1 {\n        ((limit_raw \u003c\u003c 12) | 0xFFF) as u32\n    } else {\n        limit_raw as u32\n    };\n\n    // Access byte (byte 5): type(4) | S(1) | DPL(2) | P(1)\n    let access = ((raw \u003e\u003e 40) \u0026 0xFF) as u8;\n    let type_ = access \u0026 0x0F;\n    let s = (access \u003e\u003e 4) \u0026 1;\n    let dpl = (access \u003e\u003e 5) \u0026 3;\n    let present = (access \u003e\u003e 7) \u0026 1;\n\n    // Flags nibble (high nibble of byte 6): AVL(1) | L(1) | D/B(1) | G(1)\n    let flags = ((raw \u003e\u003e 52) \u0026 0x0F) as u8;\n    let long_mode = (flags \u003e\u003e 1) \u0026 1;\n    let db = (flags \u003e\u003e 2) \u0026 1;\n\n    SegmentDescriptor {\n        base,\n        limit,\n        selector,\n        type_,\n        s,\n        dpl,\n        present,\n        long_mode,\n        db,\n        granularity,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a minimal inactive segment descriptor (present=0) for TR/LDT.\nconst fn null_segment(selector: u16) -\u003e SegmentDescriptor {\n    SegmentDescriptor {\n        base: 0,\n        limit: 0,\n        selector,\n        type_: 0,\n        s: 0,\n        dpl: 0,\n        present: 0,\n        long_mode: 0,\n        db: 0,\n        granularity: 0,\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Build a 64-bit TSS descriptor as two 8-byte GDT entries.\n///\n/// A 64-bit TSS descriptor is 16 bytes, spanning two consecutive GDT slots.\n/// The low 8 bytes follow the same layout as a 32-bit system descriptor;\n/// the high 8 bytes contain the upper 32 bits of the base address.\nconst fn build_tss_descriptor(base: u64, limit: u64) -\u003e (u64, u64) {\n    let base_lo = base \u0026 0xFFFF;\n    let base_mid = (base \u003e\u003e 16) \u0026 0xFF;\n    let base_hi = (base \u003e\u003e 24) \u0026 0xFF;\n    let base_upper = base \u003e\u003e 32;\n\n    let limit_lo = limit \u0026 0xFFFF;\n    let limit_hi = (limit \u003e\u003e 16) \u0026 0xF;\n\n    // Access byte: type=0x9 (64-bit TSS available), S=0, DPL=0, P=1 → 0x89\n    // Flags nibble: G=0, limit_hi\n    let low = limit_lo\n        | (base_lo \u003c\u003c 16)\n        | (base_mid \u003c\u003c 32)\n        | (0x89 \u003c\u003c 40) // access byte\n        | (limit_hi \u003c\u003c 48)\n        | (base_hi \u003c\u003c 56);\n\n    let high = base_upper; // upper 32 bits of base, rest reserved (zero)\n\n    (low, high)\n}\n\n/// Write the GDT entries into guest memory at [`GDT_GPA`].\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Bootstraps the Global Descriptor Table (GDT) directly into guest memory.\n/// This enables the VM to transition seamlessly into 64-bit long mode.\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use hitz_vmm::GuestMemory;\n/// use hitz_vmm::boot_regs::{write_gdt, GDT_GPA};\n/// use 64-bit TSS).\n/// Returns a `MemError` if the intended memory region is not mapped.\npub fn write_gdt(mem: \u0026GuestMemory) -\u003e Result\u003c(), MemError\u003e {\n    let (tss_low, tss_high) = build_tss_descriptor(TSS_GPA, TSS_SIZE - 1);\n    let entries = [GDT_NULL, GDT_CODE64, GDT_DATA64, tss_low, tss_high];\n    for (i, \u0026entry) in entries.iter().enumerate() {\n        let gpa = Gpa::new(GDT_GPA + (i * GDT_ENTRY_SIZE) as u64);\n        mem.write_u64(gpa, entry)?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Configure a vCPU's special registers for 64-bit long mode with the given\n/// page ..StandardRegs::default()\n    };\n\n    vcpu.set_regs(\u0026regs)\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n VM lifecycle management for Hitz.\n//!\n//! # Abstract\n//!\n//! This module serves as the orchestrator for the Hitz micro-VM lifecycle. It bridges\n//! the gap between abstract configuration (found in `hitz-api`) and raw hypervisor\n//! execution (provided by `hitz-whp` and `hitz-hal`).\n//!\n//! By handling vCPU threads, guest memory allocation, the Linux boot sequence (including\n//! setting up page tables via `boot_regs`), and routing device I/O through a shared\n//! memory bus, it ensures a seamless experience when booting micro-VMs.\n//!\n//! # The Hero's Journey\n//!\n//! To start a VM, one typically uses the [`boot_and_run`] function, supplying a configuration\n//! and necessary file paths. Here is a conceptual snippet showing how the VM boot sequence\n//! operates under the hood:\n//!\n//! ```no_run\n//! use hitz_api::VmConfig;\n//! use hitz_vmm::{boot_and_run, VmRunResult};\n//! use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};\n//! use std::sync::Arc;\n//!\n//! // 1. Define the VM configuration\n//! let config = VmConfig {\n//!     ram_mib: 256,\n//!     cpus: 1,\n//!     kernel_path: std::path::PathBuf::from(\"vmlinux\"),\n//!     initramfs_path: None,\n//!     disk_path: None,\n//!     cmdline: None,\n//!     net: None,\n//!     ports: vec![],\n//!     guest_cid: 3,\n//!     guest_agent: Default::default(),\n//! };\n//!\n//! // 2. Create a cancellation flag\n//! let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));\n//!\n//! // 3. Boot and run the VM\n//! // In practice, you would provide paths to the kernel and initramfs.\n//! // let result = boot_and_run::\u003cHitzWhpHypervisor, _\u003e(\u0026config, \u0026config, None, cancel, BootExtras::default());\n//! // match result {\n//! //     Ok(VmRunResult::Exited(reason)) =\u003e println!(\"VM gracefully exited: {:?}\", reason),\n//! //     Ok(VmRunResult::Cancelled) =\u003e println!(\"VM was forcefully stopped\"),\n//! //     Err(e) =\u003e eprintln!(\"Failed to run VM: {:?}\", e),\n//! // }\n//! ```\n//!\n//! # The Fine Print\n//!\n//! - **Guest Memory**: Guest memory uses raw pointers from Windows `VirtualAlloc`. This is\n//!   inherent to the design of the Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHP) and requires `unsafe`\n//!   code. Memory must be carefully mapped and unmapped to avoid access violations.\n//! - **CPU Limits**: The number of vCPUs is bounded by the host's capabilities and WHP\n//!   limitations. 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,  // mov [rbx+0xA4], 0        (QueueUsedHigh)\n        0xC7, 0x43, 0x44, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,              // mov [rbx+0x44], 1 (QueueReady)\n\n        // ---- Trigger block read (QueueNotify at offset 0x50) ----\n        0xC7, 0x43, 0x50, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,              // mov [rbx+0x50], 0\n\n        // ---- Post-interrupt: \"D\" to serial, status byte, halt ----\n                           // out dx, al\n        0xB9, 0x00, 0x50, 0x20, 0x00,                          // mov ecx, 0x205000\n        0x8A, 0x01,                                              // mov structures (same as Phase 3) ──\n    let desc0 = build_descriptor(0x20_3000, 16, 1 /* NEXT */, 1);\n    let desc1 = build_descriptor(0x20_4000, 512, 3 /* NEXT|WRITE */, 2);\n    let desc2 =        Some(0),\n        \"last byte should be status OK (0), got: {output:?}\"\n    );\n}\n\n/// Phase 4 checkpoint: Boot a real vmlinux with initramfs.\n///\n/// This is the end-to-end test for This module provides the tools necessary to evaluate the current health\n//! of a system based on its telemetry metrics. self.cpu.total_pct));\n        } else if self.cpu.total_pct \u003e 75.0 {\n            if status == HealthStatus::Healthy {\n                status = HealthStatus::Warning;\n            }\n            reasons.push(format!(\"High CPU usage: {:.1}%\", self.cpu.total_pct));\n        }\n\n        // Memory evaluation\n        if self.memory.total_bytes \u003e 0 {\n            let memory_pct =\n                (self.memory.used_bytes as f64 / self.memory.total_bytes as f64) * 100.0;\n            if memory_pct \u003e 90.0 {\n                status = HealthStatus::Critical;\n                reasons.push(format!(\"Critical memory usage: {memory_pct:.1}%\"));\n            } else if memory_pct \u003e 75.0 {\n                if status == HealthStatus::Healthy {\n                    status = HealthStatus::Warning;\n                }\n                reasons.push(format!(\"High memory usage: {memory_pct:.1}%\"));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Swap evaluation\n        if reasons.push(format!(\"Critical network errors: {total_net_errors}\"));\n        } else if total_net_errors \u003e 10 {\n            if status == HealthStatus::Healthy {\n                status = HealthStatus::Warning;\n            }\n            reasons.push(format!(\"Elevated network errors: {total_net_errors}\"));\n        }\n\n        SystemHealth { status, reasons }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::{CpuMetrics, MemoryMetrics, NetMetrics};\n\n    fn safe_metrics() -\u003e MetricsSnapshot {\n        MetricsSnapshot {\n #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]\n    fn to_prometheus(\u0026self, vm_id: \u0026str) -\u003e String {\n        use core::fmt::Write;\n\n        // Pre-allocate a reasonable buffer size to avoid dynamic reallocation.\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(2048);\n        let ts = self.timestamp_ms;\n\n        // Helper macro to append a metric line using `write!` to avoid intermediate String allocations.\n        macro_rules! metric {\n            ($name:expr, $type:expr, $help:expr, $val:expr) =\u003e {\n                let _ = writeln!(out, \"# HELP {} {}\", $name, $help);\n                let _ = writeln!(out, \"# TYPE {} {}\", $name, $type);\n                let _ = writeln!(out, \"{}{{vm_id=\\\"{}\\\"}} {} {}\", $name, vm_id, $val, ts);\n            };\n            ($name:expr, $type:expr, $help:expr, $labels:expr, $val:expr) =\u003e {\n                let _ = writeln!(out, \"# HELP {} {}\", $name, $help);\n                let _ = writeln!(out, \"# TYPE {} {}\", $name, $type);\n                let _ = writeln!(\n                    out,\n                    \"{}{{vm_id=\\\"{}\\\",{}}} {} {}\",\n                    $name, vm_id, $labels, $val, ts\n                );\n            };\n        }\n\n        // --- CPU Metrics ---\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_cpu_total_pct\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Overall CPU utilisation percentage\",\n            self.cpu.total_pct\n        );\n\n        for (i, core_pct) in self.cpu.per_core.iter().enumerate() {\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_cpu_core_pct\",\n                \"gauge\",\n                \"Per-core CPU utilisation percentage\",\n                format!(\"core=\\\"{}\\\"\", i),\n                core_pct\n            );\n        }\n\n        metric!(\n metric!(\n            \"hitz_cpu_load_avg\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"System load average over 5 minutes\",\n            \"window=\\\"5m\\\"\",\n            self.cpu.load_avg[1]\n        );\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_cpu_load_avg\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"System load average over 15 minutes\",\n            \"window=\\\"15m\\\"\",\n            self.cpu.load_avg[2]\n        );\n\n        // --- Memory Metrics ---\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_total_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Total physical memory in self.memory.used_bytes\n        );\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_free_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Free memory in bytes\",\n            self.memory.free_bytes\n        );\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_buffers_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Memory used for buffers in bytes\",\n            self.memory.buffers_bytes\n        );\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_cached_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Memory used for page cache in bytes\",\n            self.memory.cached_bytes\n        );\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_swap_total_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Total swap space in bytes\",\n            self.memory.swap_total\n        );\n        metric!(\n            \"hitz_memory_swap_used_bytes\",\n            \"gauge\",\n            \"Swap space in use in bytes\",\n            self.memory.swap_used\n        );\n\n        // --- Disk Metrics ---\n        for disk in \u0026self.disks {\n            let labels = format!(\"device=\\\"{}\\\"\", disk.name);\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_disk_reads_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total completed read operations\",\n                labels,\n                disk.reads_total\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_disk_writes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total completed write operations\",\n                labels,\n                disk.writes_total\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_disk_read_bytes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total bytes read\",\n                labels,\n                disk.read_bytes\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_disk_write_bytes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total bytes written\",\n                labels,\n                disk.write_bytes\n            );\n        }\n\n        // --- Network Metrics ---\n        for net in \u0026self.networks {\n            let labels = format!(\"interface=\\\"{}\\\"\", net.interface);\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_net_rx_bytes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total bytes received\",\n                labels,\n                net.rx_bytes\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_net_tx_bytes_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total bytes transmitted\",\n                labels,\n                net.tx_bytes\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_net_rx_packets_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total packets received\",\n                labels,\n                net.rx_packets\n               net.rx_errors\n            );\n            metric!(\n                \"hitz_net_tx_errors_total\",\n                \"counter\",\n                \"Total transmit errors\",\n    clippy::unwrap_used,\n    clippy::expect_used,\n    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,\n    clippy::identity_op\n)]\n//! Identity-mapped x86-64 page table generation.\n//!\n//! Builds 4-level page tables using 2 MiB huge pages. The output is a\n//! sequence of [`MemWrite`] chunks that the caller writes into guest\n//! physical memory — `hitz-boot` never touches guest RAM directly.\n\nuse hitz_hal::Gpa;\n\nuse crate::error::BootError;\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Public types\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// A chunk of data to write into guest memory.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct MemWrite {\n    /// Guest physical address where the data should be written.\n    pub gpa: Gpa,\n    /// Raw bytes to write at `gpa`.\n    pub data: Vec\u003cu8\u003e,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Constants\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Guest physical address of the PML4 table.\npub const PML4_GPA: u64 = 0x8000;\n/// Guest physical address of the PDPT table.\npub const PDPT_GPA: u64 = 0x9000;\n/// Guest physical address of the first Page Directory table.\npub const PD_BASE_GPA: u64 = 0xA000;\n\n/// Page is present in memory.\nconst PAGE_PRESENT: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 0;\n/// Page is read/write.\nconst PAGE_RW: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 1;\n/// PS bit — marks a 2 MiB huge page in a PD entry.\nconst PAGE_SIZE_FLAG: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 7;\n\n/// Flags for a table entry that points to a child table (PML4 -\u003e PDPT, PDPT -\u003e PD).\nconst TABLE_FLAGS: u64 = PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_RW; // 0x3\n/// Flags for a 2 MiB huge page leaf entry in a PD table.\nconst HUGE_PAGE_FLAGS: u64 = PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_RW | PAGE_SIZE_FLAG; // 0x83\n\n/// Size of a single page table (4 KiB).\nconst PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;\n/// Number of 8-byte entries per page table.\nconst ENTRIES_PER_TABLE: usize = 512;\n/// Size of a 2 MiB huge page in bytes.\nconst HUGE_PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 2 * 1024 * 1024;\n/// Size of 1 GiB in bytes.\nconst ONE_GIB: u64 = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;\n/// Maximum GiB count supported (PDPT has 512 entries, each mapping 1 GiB).\nconst MAX_GIB: u32 = 512;\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Public API\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Build identity-mapped page tables for `gib_count` GiB of physical memory.\n///\n/// Returns `(pml4_gpa, writes)` where `pml4_gpa` is the address to load into\n/// CR3 and `writes` is the set of page-table pages to write into guest RAM.\n///\n/// Uses 2 MiB huge pages so only three levels are needed:\n/// PML4 -\u003e PDPT -\u003e PD (with PS bit set).\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns [`BootError::InvalidPageTableConfig`] if `gib_count` is zero or\n/// exceeds 512 (the maximum a single PDPT can map).\npub fn build_page_tables(gib_count: u32) -\u003e Result\u003c(Gpa, Vec\u003cMemWrite\u003e), BootError\u003e {\n    if gib_count == 0 || gib_count \u003e MAX_GIB {\n        return Err(BootError::InvalidPageTableConfig(format!(\n            \"gib_count must be in 1..={MAX_GIB}, got {gib_count}\"\n        )));\n    }\n\n    // Total writes: 1 PML4 + 1 PDPT + gib_count PD tables.\n    let total_writes = 2 + gib_count as usize;\n    let mut writes = Vec::with_capacity(total_writes);\n\n    // -- PML4 (one entry pointing at the PDPT) ----------------------------\n    let mut pml4 = vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE];\n    write_entry(\u0026mut pml4, 0, PDPT_GPA | TABLE_FLAGS);\n    writes.push(MemWrite {\n        gpa: Gpa::new(PML4_GPA),\n        data: pml4,\n    });\n\n    // -- PDPT (one entry per GiB, each pointing at a PD table) ------------\n    let mut pdpt = vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE];\n    for i in 0..gib_count {\n        let pd_gpa = PD_BASE_GPA + u64::from(i) * PAGE_SIZE as u64;\n        write_entry(\u0026mut pdpt, i as usize, pd_gpa | TABLE_FLAGS);\n    }\n    writes.push(MemWrite {\n        gpa: Gpa::new(PDPT_GPA),\n        data: pdpt,\n    });\n\n    // -- PD tables (512 x 2 MiB huge-page entries each) -------------------\n    for i in 0..gib_count {\n        let mut pd = vec![0u8; PAGE_SIZE];\n        for j in 0..ENTRIES_PER_TABLE {\n            let phys_addr = u64::from(i) * ONE_GIB + j as u64 * HUGE_PAGE_SIZE;\n            write_entry(\u0026mut pd, j, phys_addr | HUGE_PAGE_FLAGS);\n        }\n        writes.push(MemWrite {\n            gpa: Gpa::new(PD_BASE_GPA + u64::from(i) * PAGE_SIZE as u64),\n            data: pd,\n        });\n    }\n\n    Ok((Gpa::new(PML4_GPA), writes))\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Write a 64-bit little-endian value into the `index`-th slot of a page table.\nfn write_entry(table: \u0026mut [u8], index: usize, value: u64) {\n    let offset = index * 8;\n    table[offset..offset + 8].copy_from_slice(\u0026value.to_le_bytes());\n}\n\n/// Read a 64-bit little-endian value from the `index`-th slot of a page table.\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn read_entry(table: \u0026[u8], index: usize) -\u003e u64 {\n    let offset = index * 8;\n    u64::from_le_bytes(table[offset..offset + 8].try_into().expect(\"8 bytes\"))\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Tests\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_4gib_page_tables() {\n        let (cr3, writes) = build_page_tables(4).expect(\"4 GiB should succeed\");\n\n        // 1 PML4 + 1 PDPT + 4 PD = 6 writes\n      completion_tx: tx,\n            completion_rx: Arc::new(tokio::sync::Mutex::new(rx)),\n            vm_count,\n            shutdown_rx,\n            shutdown_tx_owned: Arc::new(shutdown_tx),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Clones an existing VM configuration into a new VM.\n    ///\n    /// The source VM can be in any state. The new VM will be created in the `Created` state,\n    /// identical in configuration to the source, but with the new `dest_id`.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns a [`DaemonError`] if the source VM does not exist, or if the destination\n    /// VM ID already exists.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// manager.clone_vm(\"my-vm\", \"my-vm-clone\").expect(\"Failed to clone VM\");\n    /// ```\n    pub fn clone_vm(\u0026self, src_id: \u0026str, dest_id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let config = {\n            self.vms\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?\n                .get(src_id)\n                .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(src_id.to_string()))?\n                .config\n                .clone()\n        };\n\n        self.create_vm(dest_id.to_string(), \u0026config)\n    }\n\n    /// Wires the vsock metrics tasks to stop when a daemon-provided shutdown signal fires.\n    ///\n    /// **Why do we need a shutdown receiver?**\n    /// A running VM might have a background task pumping metrics over a vsock channel.\n    /// If the daemon needs to shut down cleanly, it must signal these background tasks\n    /// to exit their polling loops; otherwise, the Tokio runtime will hang waiting for them.\n    ///\n    /// Call this after constructing the manager. If not called, the manager uses a dummy internal\n    /// channel that never fires, which is acceptable for standalone or test execution.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let mut manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// let (shutdown_tx, shutdown_rx) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(false);\n    /// manager.set_shutdown_receiver(shutdown_rx);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn set_shutdown_receiver(\u0026mut self, rx: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver\u003cbool\u003e) {\n        self.shutdown_rx = rx;\n    }\n\n    /// Creates a VM with the given ID and configuration.\n    ///\n    /// This validates the [`VmConfig`] and persists it to disk. It does **not** boot the VM.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns a [`DaemonError`] if a VM with the same ID already exists, if the configuration\n    /// is invalid, or if the state \u0026config).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn create_vm(\u0026self, id: String, config: \u0026VmConfig) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        if id.contains('/') || id.contains('\\\\') || id.contains(\"..\") {\n            return Err(DaemonError::Internal(\"Invalid VM ID\".to_string()));\n        }\n\n        hitz_vmm::validate_config(config)?;\n\n        let info = {\n            let mut vms = self\n                .vms\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n\n            if vms.contains_key(\u0026id) {\n                return Err(DaemonError::AlreadyExists(id));\n            }\n\n            let entry = VmEntry {\n                config: config.clone(),\n info = entry.to_info(\u0026id);\n            let _ = vms.insert(id.clone(), entry);\n            info\n            // Mutex released here — filesystem I/O must not hold it.\n        };\n\n        if in-memory insert so a retry doesn't hit AlreadyExists.\n            if let Ok(mut vms) = self.vms.lock() {\n                let _ = vms.remove(\u0026id);\n            }\n            return Err(e);\n        }\n        Ok(info)\n    }\n\n    /// Boots a previously created VM.\n    ///\n    /// Transitions a `Created` VM into the `Running` state. ```\n    #[allow(clippy::significant_drop_tightening, clippy::too_many_lines)]\n    pub fn start_vm(\u0026self, id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let (config, stop_flag, serial_buf, info) = {\n            let mut vms = self\n                .vms\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n            let entry = vms\n                .get_mut(id)\n                .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(id.to_string()))?;\n\n            if entry.state != VmState::Created {\n                return Err(DaemonError::InvalidState {\n                    id: id.to_string(),\n                    state: entry.state,\n                    expected: \"Created\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n\n            let flag = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));\n            entry.stop_flag = Some(flag.clone());\n            entry.state = VmState::Running;\n\n            let serial_buf = SerialBuf::new();\n            entry.serial_buf = Some(serial_buf.clone());\n\n            (entry.config.clone(), flag, serial_buf, entry.to_info(id))\n        };\n        // Mutex released here — spawn_blocking must not hold it.\n\n        // Persist Running state before spawning the VM task.\n        self.store.save_state(id, VmState::Running)?;\n\n        // Inject guest agent overlay into initramfs if agent is enabled.\n        let boot_config = inject_guest_agent(config, id);\n\n        // Record guest RAM size as a one-shot gauge.\n        {\n            let meter = opentelemetry::global::meter(\"hitz\");\n            let memory_gauge = meter\n                .u64_gauge(\"hitz.vm.memory_bytes\")\n                .with_description(\"Guest RAM in bytes at VM start\")\n                .build();\n            memory_gauge.record(\n                u64::from(boot_config.ram_mib) * 1024 * 1024,\n                \u0026[KeyValue::new(\"vm.id\", id.to_string())],\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Increment the running-VM count.\n        self.vm_count.add(1, \u0026[KeyValue::new(\"state\", \"running\")]);\n\n        let hv = self.hypervisor.clone();\n        let vms = self.vms.clone();\n        let vm_id = id.to_string();\n        let completion_tx = self.completion_tx.clone();\n        let vm_count_clone = Arc::clone(\u0026self.vm_count);\n        let vm_id_span = vm_id.clone();\n\n        // Create vsock channels if agent injection is enabled.\n        // The host-facing ends are consumed by the async metrics task;\n        // the device-facing ends are passed to boot_and_run via BootExtras.\n        // On-demand pull is a future enhancement; only push-to-OTel is wired here.\n        let extras = if matches!(\n            boot_config.guest_agent,\n            hitz_api::GuestAgentMode::Auto | hitz_api::GuestAgentMode::Custom(_)\n        ) {\n            let (handle, rx_receiver, tx_sender) = hitz_vmm::VsockIoHandle::new_pair();\n            // Spawn the async metrics task with the host-facing channel ends.\n            // The task runs until the channels close (VM exit) or shutdown.\n            let shutdown_rx = self.shutdown_rx.clone();\n            drop(tokio::spawn(crate::vsock_server::run_metrics_task(\n                vm_id.clone(),\n                handle.tx_rx,\n                handle.rx_tx,\n                shutdown_rx,\n            )));\n            hitz_vmm::BootExtras {\n                vsock_channels: Some((rx_receiver, tx_sender)),\n            }\n        } else {\n            hitz_vmm::BootExtras::none()\n        };\n\n        let store_exit = Arc::clone(\u0026self.store);\n\n        // Fire-and-forget: the spawned task updates VM state on completion\n        // and signals the completion channel so `stop_all_and_wait` can drain.\n        drop(tokio::task::spawn(async move {\n            let boot_span = tracing::info_span!(\n                \"vm.boot\",\n                vm.id = %vm_id_span,\n                vm.ram_mib = boot_config.ram_mib,\n                vm.cpus = boot_config.cpus,\n            );\n            let _boot_enter = boot_span.enter();\n\n            // Start port forwarders if networking is configured and rules exist.\n            let _port_fwd = start_port_forwarding(\u0026boot_config).await;\n\n            let result = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {\n                hitz_vmm::boot_and_run(\u0026*hv, \u0026boot_config, serial_buf, stop_flag, extras)\n            })\n            .await;\n\n            // _port_fwd drops here → all listener tasks aborted.\n\n            // Decrement the running-VM count now that the VM has exited.\n            vm_count_clone.add(-1, \u0026[KeyValue::new(\"state\", \"running\")]);\n\n            // Update state based on result.\n            if let Ok(mut vms) = vms.lock() {\n                if let Some(entry) = vms.get_mut(\u0026vm_id) {\n                    match result {\n                        Ok(Ok(run_result)) =\u003e match run_result.exit_reason {\n                            ExitReason::Halt | ExitReason::Shutdown | ExitReason::Canceled =\u003e {\n                                entry.state = VmState::Stopped;\n                                entry.exit_reason = Some(format!(\"{:?}\", run_result.exit_reason));\n                            }\n                            ExitReason::Unexpected(ref reason) =\u003e {\n                                entry.state = VmState::Failed;\n                                entry.exit_reason = Some(reason.clone());\n                            }\n                        },\n                        Ok(Err(e)) =\u003e {\n                            entry.state = VmState::Failed;\n                            entry.exit_reason = Some(e.to_string());\n                        }\n                        Err(e) =\u003e {\n                            entry.state = VmState::Failed;\n                            entry.exit_reason = Some(format!(\"task panicked: {e}\"));\n                        }\n                    }\n                    entry.stop_flag = None;\n                    entry.vsock_handle = None;\n                    if let Some(ref buf) = entry.serial_buf {\n                        buf.close();\n                    }\n                    let final_state = entry.state;\n                    drop(vms); // explicit drop — persist state outside the lock\n                    if let Err(e) = store_exit.save_state(\u0026vm_id, final_state) {\n                        tracing::warn!(vm_id = %vm_id, error = %e, \"failed to persist VM exit state\");\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Notify stop_all_and_wait that this VM has finished.\n            let _ = completion_tx.send(vm_id);\n        }));\n\n        Ok(info)\n    }\n\n    /// Stops a running VM by setting its atomic stop flag.\n    ///\n    /// **Why an atomic flag?**\n    /// The vCPU is deeply buried inside a synchronous run loop on a separate thread.\n    /// We can't simply `await` it to stop. Instead, we flip an atomic boolean.\n    /// A cancel-watchdog thread checks this flag and issues a hypervisor-level cancellation\n    /// to yank the vCPU back to reality.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, self\n            .vms\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n        let entry = vms\n            .get_mut(id)\n            .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(id.to_string()))?;\n\n        if entry.state != VmState::Running {\n            return Err(DaemonError::InvalidState {\n                id: id.to_string(),\n                state: entry.state,\n                expected: \"Running\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref flag) = entry.stop_flag {\n            flag.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        }\n\n        let info = entry.to_info(id);\n        drop(vms);\n        Ok(info)\n    }\n\n    /// Restarts a running VM by stopping it, waiting for it to stop, and then starting it again.\n    pub async fn restart_vm(\u0026self, id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cVmInfo, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let _ = self.stop_vm(id)?;\n\n        let mut stopped = false;\n \"VM {id} failed to stop within 5 seconds for restart\"\n            )));\n        }\n\n        self.start_vm(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Gets a serial output reader for a running VM.\n    ///\n    /// When the VM is stopped\n    /// or hasn't started, the buffer doesn't exist.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// let mut reader = manager.serial_reader(\"my-vm\").unwrap();\n    /// // Stream chunks to the client...\n    /// ```\n    pub fn serial_reader(\u0026self, id: \u0026str) -\u003e Result\u003cSerialReader, DaemonError\u003e {\n        let vms = self\n            .vms\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| DaemonError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;\n        let entry = vms\n            .get(id)\n            .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::NotFound(id.to_string()))?;\n        let reader = entry\n            .serial_buf\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(SerialBuf::reader)\n            .ok_or_else(|| DaemonError::InvalidState {\n                id: id.to_string(),\n                state: entry.state,\n                expected: \"Running (with serial buffer)\".to_string(),\n            })?;\n        drop(vms);\n        Ok(reader)\n    }\n\n    /// Gets detailed information about a single VM.\n    ///\n    /// ## Returns immediately without waiting\n    /// for the VMs to reach a terminal state.\n    ///\n    /// Use [`VmManager::stop_all_and_wait`] if you need to block until all VMs have stopped.\n    ///\n    /// ## Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust,no_run\n    /// # use std::sync::Arc;\n    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;\n    /// # use hitz_daemon::VmManager;\n    /// # use hitz_whp::WhpHypervisor;\n    /// #\n    /// # let hypervisor = Arc::new(WhpHypervisor::new().unwrap());\n    /// # let state_dir = PathBuf::from(\"C:\\\\hitz\\\\vms\");\n    /// # let manager = VmManager::new(hypervisor, state_dir).unwrap();\n    /// use std::time::Duration;\n    /// # let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build().unwrap();\n    /// # rt.block_on(async {\n    /// manager.stop_all_and_wait(Duration::from_secs(5)).await;\n    /// # });\n    /// ```\n    pub async fn stop_all_and_wait(\u0026self, timeout: Duration) {\n        let running_count = {\n            let Ok(vms) = self.vms.lock() else { return };\n            let mut count = 0usize;\n            for entry in vms.values() {\n                if entry.state == VmState::Running {\n                    if let Some(ref flag) = entry.stop_flag {\n                        flag.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n                    }\n                    count += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            count\n        };\n\n        if running_count == 0 {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(running_count, \"waiting for VMs to stop\");\n\n        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + timeout;\n        let mut rx = self.completion_rx.lock().await;\n        let mut stopped = 0usize;\n\n        while stopped \u003c running_count {\n            match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, rx.recv()).await {\n                Ok(Some(_vm_id)) =\u003e {\n                    stopped += 1;\n                }\n                Ok(None) =\u003e break, // channel closed — no more senders\n                Err(_elapsed) =\u003e {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        remaining = running_count - stopped,\n                        \"timeout waiting for VMs to stop\"\n                    );\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// On-demand metrics pull. response — requires storing a dedicated pull channel end in\n    /// `VmEntry` separate from the push stream read by `run_metrics_task`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn request_metrics_snapshot(\n Currently supported devices include a 16550A-compatible serial console ([`SerialDevice`]),\n//! a virtio-block storage backend ([`VirtioBlockDevice`]), and a virtio-net network interface ([`VirtioNetDevice`]).\n//!\n//! # The Hero's Journey\n//!\n//! Devices are instantiated during the VM setup phase and registered with the central `MmioBus`.\n//! Here is a simplified illustration of how devices are attached to the bus:\n//!\n//! ```no_run\n//! use hitz_devices::{MmioBus, SerialDevice, VirtioBlockDevice, VirtioMmioTransport};\n//! use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n//!\n//! // 1. Create devices\n//! let mut serial = SerialDevice::new(std::io::sink());\n//! let block_backend = VirtioBlockDevice::new(std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/null\").unwrap()).unwrap();\n//! let mut block_device = VirtioMmioTransport::new(block_backend, std::sync::Arc::new(DummyMem), 5);\n//!\n\n//! // 3. When a guest access occurs (intercepted by WHP), route it:\n//! // e.g., guest writes 'A' (0x41) to the serial port\n//! bus.write(0x3f8, \u0026[0x41], \u0026DummyMem);\n//! ```\n//!\n//! # The Fine Print\n//!\n//! - **Virtio Over MMIO**: Hitz prefers the virtio-MMIO transport over PCI for simplicity\n//!   and reduced surface area. The kernel must be compiled with `CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO`\n//!   enabled, and device memory regions must be passed to the kernel via command line\n//! Device ID: 1 (virtio net device).\n\nuse std::collections::VecDeque;\n\nuse crossbeam_channel::{Receiver, Sender};\nuse hitz_hal::GuestMemAccess;\n\nuse crate::virtio::mmio_transport::VirtioBackend;\nuse crate::virtio::queue::VirtQueue;\n\n/// Size of the virtio-net header prepended to every frame.\nconst VIRTIO_NET_HDR_SIZE: usize = 12;\n\n/// Feature bit: device has a given MAC address in config space.\nconst VIRTIO_NET_F_MAC: u64 = 1 \u003c\u003c 5;\n\n/// RX virtqueue index (guest receives frames here).\nconst RX_QUEUE: u16 = 0;\n\n/// TX virtqueue index (guest sends frames here).\nconst TX_QUEUE: u16 = 1;\n\n/// A virtio-net device implementation.\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Provides a paravirtualized network interface to the guest OS. It uses two\n/// virtqueues: one for receiving packets (RX) and one for transmitting packets (TX).\n///\n/// This structure bridges the guest's memory buffers with host-side crossbeam\n/// channels, allowing an asynchronous host network thread to inject received ethernet\n/// frames and drain transmitted frames.\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use hitz_devices::VirtioNetDevice;\n/// # use crossbeam_channel::unbounded;\n/// # use hitz_devices::VirtioMmioTransport;\n/// # use hitz_hal::GuestMemAccess;\n/// # use std::sync::Arc;\n/// # struct DummyMem;\n/// # impl GuestMemAccess for DummyMem {\n/// #     fn read_guest(\u0026self, _gpa: u64, _buf: \u0026mut [u8]) -\u003e Result\u003c(), hitz_hal::HalError\u003e { Ok(()) }\n/// #     fn write_guest(\u0026self, _gpa: u64, _data: \u0026[u8]) -\u003e Result\u003c(), hitz_hal::HalError\u003e { Ok(()) }\n/// # }\n/// // 1. GuestMemAccess) {\n        // ⚡ Bolt: Hoist buffer to eliminate multiple heap allocations per transmitted frame.\n        let mut frame_data = Vec::with_capacity(2048);\n        while let Some(mut chain) = queue.pop_chain(mem) {\n            let head = chain.head_index();\n            frame_data.clear();\n\n            // Collect all device-readable buffers in the chain.\n            while let Some(desc) = chain.next_descriptor(mem) {\n                if !desc.is_device_writable {\n                    let start_len = frame_data.len();\n                    frame_data.resize(start_len + -\u003e bool {\n        let Some(raw_frame) = self.rx_pending.front() else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        let Some(mut chain) = queue.pop_chain(mem) else {\n            return Shared types for the HAL: exit reasons, register state, configuration.\n\nuse crate::newtypes::{Gpa, MemSizeMiB, VcpuId};\n\n/// Configuration for creating a new partition.\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Defines the fundamental parameters required to bootstrap a new VM.\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use hitz_hal::{PartitionConfig, MemSizeMiB};\n///\n/// let config = PartitionConfig {\n///     vcpu_count: 2,\n///     memory_size: MemSizeMiB::new(1024),\n/// };\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Abstract\n///\n/// Represents the various reasons a virtual CPU might stop execution\n/// and return control to the Virtual Machine Monitor (VMM).\n///\n/// # The Hero's Journey\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use hitz_hal::VcpuExit;\n///\n/// fn handle_exit(exit: VcpuExit) {\n///     match exit {\n///         VcpuExit::Halt =\u003e println!(\"Guest halted\"),\n///         VcpuExit::Shutdown =\u003e println!(\"Guest shutting down\"),\n///         _ =\u003e println!(\"Other exit reason\"),\n///     }\n/// }\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum VcpuExit {\n    /// Guest performed an MMIO access.\n    Mmio(MmioExit),\n    /// Guest performed an I/O port access (IN/OUT instruction).\n    IoPort(IoPortExit),\n    /// Guest executed HLT.\n    Halt,\n    /// vCPU is ready to accept an interrupt injection.\n    InterruptWindow,\n    /// vCPU run was canceled via [`Vcpu::cancel`](crate::Vcpu::cancel).\n    Canceled,\n    /// Guest initiated shutdown (triple fault, etc.).\n    Shutdown,\n    /// Exit reason not recognized by this HAL version.\n    Unknown(u32),\n}\n\n/// Details of an MMIO exit.\n///\n/// # For smaller accesses, only the lower bytes are valid.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct MmioExit {\n    /// Guest physical address being accessed.\n    pub gpa: Gpa,\n    /// Data buffer — for writes, contains the value written by the guest.\n    /// For reads, the VMM fills this before resuming.\n    pub data: [u8;
